reference.title: Microbial production of multiple short-chain primary amines via retrobiosynthesis

target.condition: In-house retrobiosynthesis tool; PubChemPy MeSH Tree; RDT v1.5.1; code at bitbucket.org/kaistsystemsbiology/retro-precursor-selection.

trigger.observation: Bio-based SCPA production absent despite industrial need; retrobiosynthesis predicted single enzymatic conversion from amino-acid precursors for all 15 SCPAs.
trigger.reasoning: Design biosynthetic pathways for 15 SCPAs: retrobiosynthesis (84 reaction rules) followed by precursor selection (molecular type = amino acid; functional-group relative position matching VlmD's known substrates).

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(软): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Computational prediction (retrobiosynthesis tool + database filters); predictive, required experimental confirmation which was obtained downstream (EXP-01/02).

alternatives.approach: amino alcohols, other SCPAs and alkyl-CoA precursors - rejected: poorly characterized pathways
hydrocarbon precursors - rejected: short-chain hydrocarbon production considered harder than amino acids
tert-butylamine and aniline - dropped: no amino-acid precursor with matching functional-group positions

decision_chain.implementation_detail: Computational pathway design; no wet-lab intervention.

result.metric: 4-21 predicted precursors per SCPA; best amino-acid precursor identified for 13/15 SCPAs; tert-butylamine and aniline excluded (no suitable amino-acid precursor).
result.after: Pathway designs for 13 SCPAs; VlmD selected as proof-of-concept promiscuous decarboxylase.

decision_chain.rule: When designing biosynthetic routes for a family of structurally related chemicals in E. coli, filter retrobiosynthesis-predicted precursors to amino acids whose amine/carboxyl groups sit at the same positions relative to the reaction-center carbon as the chosen promiscuous decarboxylase's known substrates, because amino-acid metabolism sustains high precursor flux and matched functional-group geometry preserves catalytic compatibility.

target.condition: MR medium pH 7.0 + 10 g/L glucose + 2 g/L precursor; 37 C, 200 rpm, 36 h, 50 mL in 300 mL baffled flask.

trigger.observation: Retrobiosynthesis predicted EC 4.1.1.- decarboxylation of amino-acid precursors; VlmD previously reported (ref 28) to convert L-Val/L-Leu/L-Ile to three SCPAs, suggesting exploitable promiscuity.
trigger.reasoning: Establish platform strain PA01 expressing codon-optimized vlmD and test in vivo SCPA production by feeding 12 direct precursors (2 g/L each).
trigger.source_location: E. coli WL3110 (lacI- mutant of W3110)

evidence.source_location: No separate negative-control strain stated for the feeding panel in main text.

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Decision validated by measured in vivo titers for 10/12 SCPAs and by in vitro conversion data.

alternatives.approach: other EC 4.1.1.- enzymes - noted as examinable but not tested

decision_chain.implementation_detail: Transformation with pTac15-vlmDopt (heterologous codon-optimized S. viridifaciens vlmD under Ptac in pTac15K).

result.metric: SCPA titers by HPLC-OPA; residual precursor for the two failures (Supplementary Fig. 3).
result.after: 10/12 SCPAs produced in vivo (titers 76.28-1289.18 mg/L); n-amylamine and benzylamine not produced due to poor precursor utilization (L-norleucine 1.92, L-2-phenylglycine 1.82 g/L remaining of 2 g/L).

decision_chain.rule: When building a platform E. coli strain for a group of related short-chain primary amines, terminate each pathway with a single promiscuous PLP-dependent decarboxylase acting on amino-acid precursors, because irreversible decarboxylation provides a thermodynamic driving force toward amine formation.
decision_chain.calibration_reason: reason_nature 存在多个标签（Case 1），需人工确认是否两者都成立

target.condition: MR + 20 g/L glucose; 37 C, 200 rpm, 48 h flask.

trigger.observation: Feeding-based production requires externally supplied L-alanine; de novo production needs endogenous L-alanine supply from glucose.
trigger.reasoning: De novo ethylamine production from glucose.

evidence.source_location: NC01 (control strain; exact genotype requires Supplementary Table 2).

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Measured ethylamine and L-alanine titers.
decision_chain.implementation_detail: Co-overexpression of codon-optimized G. stearothermophilus alaD (alanine dehydrogenase, pyruvate -> L-alanine) with vlmDopt (strain EA01, plasmid pTac15-vlmDopt-alaDopt).

result.after: 2.89 mg/L ethylamine; 22.78 mg/L L-alanine byproduct (> ethylamine titer), attributed by authors to insufficient VlmD activity toward L-alanine.

decision_chain.rule: When producing an L-alanine-derived amine from glucose in E. coli, overexpress alanine dehydrogenase (alaD) to supply the L-alanine precursor directly from pyruvate, because alaD catalyzes reductive amination of pyruvate to L-alanine.

target.condition: NM2 medium; 30 C, 200 rpm, 48 h flask.

trigger.observation: PA01 feeding gave the highest in vivo titer for iso-butylamine (1289.18 mg/L), and an L-valine-overproducing chassis was already available.
trigger.reasoning: De novo iso-butylamine production from glucose.
trigger.source_location: E. coli Val (pKBRilvBNCED) - L-valine overproducer constructed previously (ref 21)

evidence.source_location: NC02 = Val (pKBRilvBNCED) with empty plasmid (no vlmD).

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Measured titers in flask, later confirmed in fed-batch.
decision_chain.implementation_detail: Transformation of Val (pKBRilvBNCED) with pTac15-vlmDopt (strain iBA01). The L-valine-overproducing chassis itself (ilvA/leuA/panB deletions, pKBRilvBNCED) is background from ref 21, not this paper's action.

result.after: 1155.74 mg/L (15.80 mM) iso-butylamine, no L-valine byproduct; exceeds NC02 L-valine titer (524.91 mg/L). Identified problem: Val strain auxotrophic for L-Ile, L-Leu, D-pantothenate.

target.condition: NM2 without L-leucine; 30 C, 200 rpm, 48 h flask.

trigger.observation: Iso-amylamine production requires L-leucine precursor; leuABCD genes are all involved in L-leucine biosynthesis.
trigger.reasoning: De novo iso-amylamine production from glucose.

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Measured product and byproduct titers.
decision_chain.implementation_detail: Additional overexpression of leuABCD (L-leucine biosynthesis) on pTac15-vlmDopt-pTac-leuABCD (strain iAA01).

result.metric: Iso-amylamine, L-leucine, iso-butylamine titers (Fig. 6c, Supplementary Fig. 4).
result.after: 93.23 mg/L iso-amylamine; byproducts 991.23 mg/L L-leucine and 759.89 mg/L iso-butylamine. Authors attribute L-leucine accumulation to suboptimal VlmD conversion and iso-butylamine to VlmD preference for L-valine generated from 2-ketoisovalerate (author_interpretation, 'likely/might' - not causally validated).

decision_chain.rule: When producing an L-leucine-derived amine from glucose in E. coli, overexpress the leuABCD operon to raise L-leucine precursor supply, because these genes catalyze the committed steps of L-leucine biosynthesis; note that a promiscuous decarboxylase with higher activity toward L-valine will partially divert flux to the valine-derived amine.

target.condition: 30 C; NM3 with L-Ile/L-Leu/D-pantothenate supplementation (auxotrophic host).

trigger.observation: iBA01 showed efficient iso-butylamine production without L-valine byproduct in flask cultivation.
trigger.reasoning: Enhance iso-butylamine production by scale-up of iBA01 to fed-batch.

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Measured fermentation profile.
decision_chain.implementation_detail: Fed-batch fermentation in 6.6 L bioreactor (2 L NM3), pH-stat 7.0 with ammonia, DO 40%, glucose feeding when residual glucose < 3 g/L.

result.after: 8.63 g/L iso-butylamine, productivity 0.21 g/L/h, yield 0.062 g/g (6.50-fold over flask).

target.condition: Fed-batch as EXP-06 but NM3 without L-Ile/L-Leu/D-pantothenate (medium and feed).

trigger.observation: iBA01 (Val chassis) is auxotrophic for L-Ile, L-Leu and D-pantothenate because ilvA, leuA and panB were deleted to remove competing pathways - a critical industrial bioprocess problem.
trigger.reasoning: Remove iBA01 auxotrophies while retaining competing-pathway repression, then produce iso-butylamine without supplementation.
trigger.source_location: E. coli WLGBH (pKBRilvBNCED) - parental strain of Val with intact ilvA/leuA/panB

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Measured fed-batch titer, productivity, yield and cell density improvements.

alternatives.approach: gene knockouts as in Val (pKBRilvBNCED) - rejected because they cause the auxotrophies being solved

decision_chain.implementation_detail: Synthetic sRNA knockdown of ilvA, leuA and panB via pTac15-vlmDopt-anti-ilvA-leuA-panB (strain iBA02), instead of the gene knockouts used in the Val strain.

result.after: 10.67 g/L iso-butylamine, productivity 0.36 g/L/h, yield 0.057 g/g (slightly lower than iBA01's 0.062), max OD600 60.5 (59.6% higher than iBA01's 37.9), no amino-acid/vitamin supplementation.

decision_chain.rule: When competing-pathway knockouts (ilvA, leuA, panB) cause auxotrophies in an L-valine-pathway-derived iso-butylamine production strain, replace them with synthetic sRNA-mediated knockdown of the same genes, because partial repression preserves prototrophic growth while still redirecting carbon flux toward the product.

target.condition: Flask culture as EA01 (MR + 20 g/L glucose, 37 C, 48 h).

trigger.observation: EA01 secreted more L-alanine (22.78 mg/L) than ethylamine (2.89 mg/L); VlmD showed its lowest in vitro conversion on L-alanine among the 12 working substrates.
trigger.reasoning: Improve VlmD activity toward L-alanine to enhance ethylamine production (proof-of-concept enzyme engineering).
trigger.source_location: E. coli WL3110 (12 strains, each overexpressing one vlmD variant + alaDopt)

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(软): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Mutation selection rested on a homology model (19.76% sequence identity template) and docking predictions - predictive, required experimental confirmation; confirmation then obtained by flask titers (硬 outcome data), but the design-stage evidence is predictive.
decision_chain.implementation_detail: Rational single-point mutagenesis of VlmD: homology model (SWISS-MODEL, template GAD67 PDB 2OKJ) + PLP-L-alanine docking (AutoDock Vina) identified 6 active-site residues; 12 candidate substitutions (V94I/L, V114I/L, T397A/V, W399L, S431T/V/L, D515K/N) selected from 250 BLASTP homologs; introduced by site-directed mutagenesis.

result.after: Best variant V94I: 5.69 mg/L ethylamine, +96.9% vs EA01 (2.89 mg/L); titer still low in absolute terms.

decision_chain.rule: When a PLP-dependent decarboxylase shows poor activity toward a substrate smaller than its preferred substrates, mutate active-site residues contacting the ligand to bulkier amino acids drawn from homolog-sequence variation, because reducing active-site volume increases contacts with the smaller substrate (demonstrated for VlmD/ethylamine only).

rule_provenance.rule: When designing biosynthetic routes for a family of structurally related chemicals in E. coli, filter retrobiosynthesis-predicted precursors to amino acids whose amine/carboxyl groups sit at the same positions relative to the reaction-center carbon as the chosen promiscuous decarboxylase's known substrates, because amino-acid metabolism sustains high precursor flux and matched functional-group geometry preserves catalytic compatibility.

When building a platform E. coli strain for a group of related short-chain primary amines, terminate each pathway with a single promiscuous PLP-dependent decarboxylase acting on amino-acid precursors, because irreversible decarboxylation provides a thermodynamic driving force toward amine formation.

When producing an L-alanine-derived amine from glucose in E. coli, overexpress alanine dehydrogenase (alaD) to supply the L-alanine precursor directly from pyruvate, because alaD catalyzes reductive amination of pyruvate to L-alanine.

When producing an L-leucine-derived amine from glucose in E. coli, overexpress the leuABCD operon to raise L-leucine precursor supply, because these genes catalyze the committed steps of L-leucine biosynthesis; note that a promiscuous decarboxylase with higher activity toward L-valine will partially divert flux to the valine-derived amine.

When competing-pathway knockouts (ilvA, leuA, panB) cause auxotrophies in an L-valine-pathway-derived iso-butylamine production strain, replace them with synthetic sRNA-mediated knockdown of the same genes, because partial repression preserves prototrophic growth while still redirecting carbon flux toward the product.

When a PLP-dependent decarboxylase shows poor activity toward a substrate smaller than its preferred substrates, mutate active-site residues contacting the ligand to bulkier amino acids drawn from homolog-sequence variation, because reducing active-site volume increases contacts with the smaller substrate (demonstrated for VlmD/ethylamine only).
